rationale: ffbench is a floating-point benchmark built around a small number of extremely hot, tight arithmetic loops (the static profile is empty, but the sample identity implies few functions with concentrated FP-heavy kernels), so the weight table emphasizes cheap, semantics-preserving transformations (SUB for arithmetic op diversity, SPLIT for basic-block diversity) while strongly weighting RuntimeCost and SizeCost so expensive passes such as BCF (opaque predicates in every hot block) and FLA (dispatch-loop overhead plus lost loop optimizations like vectorization) are suppressed on hot functions; CorrectnessRisk is kept high across the board because aggressive control-flow restructuring of FP reduction loops can perturb numerically sensitive code; ICALL is down-weighted since the benchmark has sparse call sites and indirect calls would block inlining in FP hot paths, while IGV and IBR are kept at moderate weight to add global data-flow and branch-target diversity at acceptable cost.
